controls.title: AI system risk classification
controls.summary: The vendor has classified its AI systems according to the Act's risk tiers (unacceptable, high, limited, minimal) and can justify the classification.
controls.validationGuidance: This is foundational - if classification hasn't been done, none of the tier-specific obligations can be verified. Treat missing classification as a significant gap, not just informational.

controls.title: Prohibited practices screening
controls.summary: The vendor has confirmed its AI systems do not engage in practices the Act prohibits outright, such as certain forms of biometric categorization or manipulative techniques.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for the specific screening performed, not just a general assurance of legal compliance.

controls.title: Risk management system for high-risk AI
controls.summary: For AI systems classified as high-risk, the vendor maintains a continuous risk management system covering the system's full lifecycle.
controls.validationGuidance: Only applicable if the vendor's system falls into a high-risk category (e.g. employment, credit, biometric ID) - mark NOT_APPLICABLE with justification otherwise.

controls.title: Data governance for high-risk AI training data
controls.summary: Training, validation, and testing data for high-risk AI systems meets quality criteria and is examined for possible biases.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for documented data governance practices specific to the high-risk system, not generic data quality statements.

controls.title: Technical documentation and record-keeping
controls.summary: The vendor maintains technical documentation sufficient to demonstrate compliance, including automatically generated logs where required.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask whether documentation is retained for the legally required period and can be produced on request, not only that it exists.

controls.title: Human oversight measures for high-risk AI
controls.summary: High-risk AI systems are designed to allow effective human oversight, including the ability for a human to intervene or halt the system.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm the oversight mechanism is practically usable within the actual operational workflow, not a theoretical capability.

controls.title: Transparency obligations toward users
controls.summary: Users are informed when they are interacting with an AI system (e.g. chatbots, deepfake content, emotion recognition) as required by the Act.
controls.validationGuidance: Check the actual user-facing disclosure, not just a clause buried in terms of service.

controls.title: Conformity assessment and CE marking (high-risk systems)
controls.summary: Where required, the vendor has completed a conformity assessment procedure and can provide evidence of CE marking for the AI system.
controls.validationGuidance: This is a formal, documented process - a vendor claiming compliance without a conformity assessment record should be flagged for follow-up.

controls.title: Post-market monitoring plan
controls.summary: The vendor has a plan to monitor the performance of high-risk AI systems after deployment and to report serious incidents to authorities as required.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a defined incident reporting threshold and timeline, not just a general monitoring statement.
